messages.subject: News update
parts:
Dear all,

Version 1.9-1
I uploaded GGIR version 1.9-1 to CRAN yesterday, it may take a few days before it is available on MacOS and Windows. This release has only a few minor bug fixes not relevant to most of you, but as the last release has already been two months ago it seemed good to create a new release. Additionally, I spent a couple of hours yesterday trying to improve the vignette. A couple of users recently indicated to me that the high number of optional arguments to function g.shell.GGIR can be overwhelming and that more guidance on it would be welcome. So, I especially worked on the section related to g.shell.GGIR. I imagine this can be improved further, but hopefully this is already a step forward relative to how it was. Feedback on how we can improve this further is definitely welcome.

GGIR overview paper accepted
A GGIR overview paper has been accepted in the Journal for the Measurement of Physical Behaviour with Jairo Migueles as first author. We hope this paper will provide an easy introduction to GGIR for new users and simplify citing GGIR in academic literature. Once it is online, we will incorporate a link to the paper in the GGIR documentation.

Consultancy service
As of this month I am full time independent consultant, available to provide consultancies related to wearable movement sensor data in the form of advise, training, or the development of methods and software.You can see this as a complementary service to the open source nature of GGIR. Altruistic community efforts to improve GGIR and to help new users are always welcome, but if you have a need for more dedicated time investments from me then this is now possible. Also, if you simply want to support me in leading and coordinating the maintenance of GGIR then the support service I launched last year is still ongoing https://movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir. At the moment my hourly price is 160 Euros (excluding service tax) for short consultancies lasting under two days. For longer consultancies I can offer reductions tailored to the duration and the type of service you require. Please get in touch for more information or see www.movementdata.nl.

Meet the team
- At the end of June the ICAMPAM conference will be held in Maastricht in The Netherlands. Jairo and I will both be there, and look forward meeting you there. Registration for the conference is still open.
- On the 6th of June I will be speaking in Oxford about GGIR at this symposium "Physical activity and rest". Note: registration deadline is on the 29th of May.

GGIR used for sleep analysis in UKBiobank
In the past 5 months a series of high profile papers were published relating to GGIR's use for sleep analysis in UK Biobank https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-09576-1, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-08259-7, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-019-0361-7, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-08917-4 . This has received a lot of media attention and is helping to grow the GGIR user community. Special thanks to the team in Exeter (Samuel Jones, Andy Wood, Michael Weedon, Tim Frayling) for leading on this and obtaining the MRC grant that paid for 6 months of my time to develop the method to detect the sleep period time window underlying all this work.

Best wishes,
Vincent
